messages:
sara (pm): Heads up — Maya flagged a customer ask from Arbiter Analytics. They want a private VPC/on-prem style deploy with HSM key wrap, strict egress rules, and an 8–12 week timeline. Can we triage scope + must-haves?

maya (sales): yes — they committed to a pilot contract if we can meet that timeline. Main asks: VPC peering, HSM integration (external vendor), cert management, and no external internet egress besides our registry.

anita (solutions): quick clarifying q: are they okay with a Redwood Private control plane (we manage) or do they insist on fully customer-managed control plane? That changes dependencies a lot.

sara (pm): they prefer customer-managed control plane but are open to hybrid if it shortens time. Priority #1 is data isolation + HSM.

liam (eng): noted. From runtime side, major items: 1) kernel/quantization testing in their infra, 2) KV cache persistence plan (we usually rely on local NVMe), 3) networking for model pulls. We also need GPU quota and driver compatibility checks.

josh (security): need SOC/compliance gating: vendor HSM attestation, KMS API review, cert rotation process, and an internal threat model for air-gapped segments. Also: legal SOW before we touch customer infra.

ops-bot: action created: #INC-4827 create private-deploy checklist (assignee: liam). Due: 3 business days.

anita (solutions): proposing two scope paths to present to Arbiter: 
- Path A (fast): Hybrid control plane, Redwood hosts control plane, customer VPC only for runtime. We handle certs via customer-managed KMS + Redwood bridge. ~6–8 weeks.
- Path B (full private): Customer-managed control plane + airgap + external HSM vendor. More work: network peering + cert pipeline + legal. ~10–14 weeks.

liam (eng): technical deps we should add to checklist:
- firewall rules: allow egress to <redwood-registry> and KMS endpoints only
- sample ip blocks: ```10.0.0.0/16 (customer VPC) -> allow r/w to 100.64.0.0/10 (control plane nat)```
- driver matrix: CUDA/ROCm versions
- storage: nvme + mount paths and IOPS

sara (pm): good. Also list minimal launch criteria for pilot: 
- HSM proof-of-concept with test key wrap
- successful model load + inference at our target 200ms p50 on pilot instance size
- cert rotation tested end-to-end
- signed SOW + security checklist completed

maya (sales): i'll get the SOW draft started and loop legal. I'll ask customer to confirm whether they can accept the hybrid control plane as a fallback.

josh (security): I'll schedule a short call with Arbiter Sec for vendor-HSM attestation and to walk through threat model. Prefer before infra work starts.

liam (eng): immediate blockers: need customer infra contact + GPU inventory and a sample AMI/container image we can test. Can we ask them for one test instance by EOW?

anita (solutions): I'll send a templated onboarding packet with required artifacts (VPC CIDRs, peering contacts, KMS/HSM endpoints, cert issuer, firewall admins).

ops-bot: task updated: #INC-4827 checklist drafted by liam. Link: https://git.internal/repo/priv-deploy-checklist/4827

sara (pm): action items summary (short):
1) Maya -> SOW + confirm hybrid fallback (due: 48h)
2) Anita -> onboarding packet to customer (due: 24h)
3) Liam -> draft runtime checklist + testing plan (due: 3 days)
4) Josh -> security call with customer (due: 3 days)
5) Ops -> reserve tentative infra window (TBD)

sara (pm): tagging @liam @anita @josh for visibility. If we can align on Path A as pilot, we should be able to hit the contract timeline. If they insist on Path B, timeline likely slips. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maya (sales): noted. i'll nudge customer and push for Path A acceptance.

liam (eng): 👍 I'll start the checklist and post a lightweight runbook snippet here once ready.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued (preview infra) — runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/preview-deploys/1967890123

sara (pm): thanks team — keeping this thread as the single source for the intake. I'll update status after customer response.
